summary: The note describes how cultural initiatives launched in Eastbank since September 2023 have boosted the neighborhood's economy and community life. It lays out a step-by-step approach: identify cultural assets, empower local talent, build partnerships, hold events, integrate culture into urban development, use technology, educate through culture, reinvest, and secure policy support. Eastbank's projects and a study showing revenue and property value gains serve as the model for other communities.
one_line: Eastbank's cultural initiatives since September 2023 boosted business revenue and property values, offering a step-by-step model for other communities.
key_facts: Cultural initiatives have proliferated in Eastbank since September 2023 and are credited with a renewed sense of community.
Sociologist Dr. Mara Elliot, who specializes in community development, says cultural initiatives 'serve as the heartbeat of a community.'
A study released on October 30, 2023 linked Eastbank's revitalization to a 15% uptick in local business revenues and a 12% rise in property values.
Eastbank's old mill district was transformed into an arts and heritage site by January 2024, hosting exhibitions, markets, and performances.
The 'Creators’ Co-op,' established in early February 2024, provides shared studio space, commercial opportunities, and exposure for local artisans.
On March 12, 2024, Eastbank's city council partnered with several non-profit cultural organizations to secure grants and investments for community projects.
The annual 'Riverfest' is part of Eastbank's cultural calendar, and a local economic impact report tied such events to spikes in hotel occupancy and retail sales.
The first phase of the Eastbank waterfront redevelopment finished on June 10, 2024, and included an outdoor amphitheater and public art installations.
The 'Cultural Compass' app launched in August 2024 to guide residents and visitors to the city's cultural hotspots and events.
The 'Eastbank History Alive!' project, launched on September 1, 2024, brings local history into classrooms.
Eastbank's Cultural Reinvestment Fund, fed by a portion of proceeds from cultural events and partnerships, sustains and scales community projects.
Mayor Claudia Thompson has enacted policies that streamline permitting for cultural events, offer tax incentives for arts-related businesses, and approve arts funding.
